title: Tiered KV-precision regimen sweep and calibration-to-latency mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Evaluate a tiered KV precision strategy (tiered FP8/INT8/hybrid) and a calibration regimen that minimizes quality regressions while delivering measurable token-per-second improvements for long-context generation. Context: KV cache quantization can shave memory and compute but interacts with KV drift and attention kernel selection. This ticket coordinates experiments to map calibration parameters to observed latency and three quality signals (embedding cosine, next-token logprob delta, and targeted behavioral test failures).
experiment_plan: Select 3 representative models: rwd-7b, rwd-13b, community-30b (FP32 baseline)
Define precision tiers: baseline FP16/FP8, conservative INT8 (per-layer scale), aggressive INT8 (per-channel symmetric), and hybrid (FP8 for keys, INT8 for values)
Calibration pipelines: offline min-max per-layer, KL-divergence per-channel, and a scheduled online drift-adjust with 24h holdout sampling
Workloads: short chat (<=256 tokens), long generation (4k+ tokens with KV reuse), and embedding-heavy rerank flow
Metrics captured: median p99 latency, tokens/sec, mean embedding cosine (vs FP32), avg next-token logprob delta, targeted eval failure rate (5 curated prompts), and memory footprint
Run controlled A/B across identical hardware (A100S x8) with 30 seeds per config to estimate variance
Log artifacts: perf traces, per-layer scale histograms, calibration traces, and model outputs for human spot-checks
success_criteria: Find at least one tiered profile that yields >=15% tokens/sec improvement vs FP16 baseline with mean embedding cosine drop <= 0.005 and next-token logprob delta within -0.15 nats on average, and no >2% increase in targeted eval failure rate. Produce a reproducible calibration recipe and binary selector heuristics for runtime to pick tier based on SLO target.
results_summary: Preliminary runs (rwd-13b): conservative INT8 reduced memory by ~28% and improved tokens/sec by 12% with mean embedding cosine drop 0.0028 and logprob delta -0.07. Aggressive INT8 gave +24% tokens/sec but embedding cosine drop rose to 0.009 (outside threshold) and targeted eval failures increased 5%. Hybrid (keys:FP8, values:INT8) hit +18% tokens/sec with embedding drop 0.0036 and logprob delta -0.11 — acceptable on majority of prompts but showed instability on long-context arithmetic prompts. Online drift-adjust calibration reduced regression rate by ~40% relative to static per-layer min-max for workloads with heterogeneous prefix distributions.
